title: The Journey to Sham, Buhayra the Monk, and Divine Protection
overview: This episode covers the young life of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ under the care of his uncle Abu Talib, including his early trade journey toward Sham at age twelve. During this trip, the Christian monk Buhayra recognized the signs of prophethood on the young boy and warned Abu Talib to return him safely to Makkah. The lecture also highlights how Allah protected Muhammad ﷺ throughout his youth from worldly immorality, exposure, and bad manners.
lessons: Divine protection surrounds those chosen by Allah long before their official calling or mission begins.
Tending sheep instills patience, humility, responsibility, and leadership qualities essential for spiritual guidance.
True nobility of character (akhlaq) is reflected in self-restraint, modesty, and consideration for others even in childhood.
Financial hardship does not diminish honor, as demonstrated by Abu Talib's generous family despite their poverty.
Pure faith naturally rejects idolatry and falsehood, even when surrounded by prevalent societal misguidance.

chapters.title: Under the Care of Abu Talib
chapters.summary: Following the deaths of his mother Aminah and grandfather Abdul Muttalib, eight-year-old Muhammad ﷺ was taken into the care of his paternal uncle Abu Talib. Abu Talib treated him with immense love and affection, often referring to him as his own son. The Prophet ﷺ grew deeply attached to his uncle, forming a strong bond during these formative years. Abu Talib raised him with great respect and affection despite his family's financial hardship.
key_points: Muhammad ﷺ lived in three households by age eight: Halimah al-Sa'diyyah, Aminah bint Wahb, and Abdul Muttalib
Paternal uncle Abu Talib took custody of Muhammad ﷺ at age eight
Abu Talib treated Muhammad ﷺ as his own child, addressing him affectionately as 'ibni' (my son)
The deep mutual love and attachment between uncle and nephew established a lifelong bond

chapters.title: The Trade Journey to Sham
chapters.summary: When Muhammad ﷺ turned twelve, Abu Talib prepared to lead a summer trade caravan up to Sham. The Quraysh customarily made two annual trade trips: south to Yemen in winter and north to Sham in summer, as referenced in Surah Quraysh. Seeing his uncle prepare to leave, young Muhammad ﷺ tearfully requested to join the expedition. Overcoming initial hesitation and the advice of his own sons, Abu Talib agreed to take his nephew along on his first major journey outside Makkah.
key_points: Quraysh conducted bi-annual trade trips: winter to Yemen and summer to Sham (Surah Quraysh)
Muhammad ﷺ was twelve years old when he requested to join Abu Talib's trade caravan
This was the Prophet's ﷺ first journey outside the greater Makkah area since early childhood
Abu Talib granted Muhammad's ﷺ tearful request despite the length and difficulty of the journey

chapters.title: Meeting Buhayra the Monk
chapters.summary: Along the trade route to Sham, the caravan halted near a Christian monastery inhabited by monks who practiced asceticism. The chief monk, Buhayra, observed a unique cloud hovering above and shielding the caravan from the harsh sun. Recognizing that something extraordinary was occurring, Buhayra invited all members of the caravan to a grand meal. The Quraysh left twelve-year-old Muhammad ﷺ behind to watch over their goods, but Buhayra insisted that every single member of the group be brought inside.
key_points: Buhayra (Bahira) was a knowledgeable Christian monk living in a monastery along the Sham trade route
Buhayra noticed a cloud continuously shading the caravan from the scorching summer heat
The monk invited the entire trade caravan for an unusual feast to inspect the travelers
Muhammad ﷺ was initially left behind to guard the luggage before Buhayra requested his presence

chapters.title: Recognition of Prophethood and Return to Makkah
chapters.summary: Upon meeting Muhammad ﷺ, Buhayra observed that he began eating with 'Bismillah' rather than invoking idols. Buhayra tested the boy by swearing by al-Lat and al-Uzza, to which Muhammad ﷺ declared his absolute hatred for those idols. Buhayra then inspected the back of Muhammad ﷺ and confirmed the physical mark of Khatam al-Nubuwwah (the Seal of Prophethood) between his shoulders. Learning that the boy was an orphan under Abu Talib's care, Buhayra warned Abu Talib to return him to Makkah immediately to protect him from hostile groups in Sham, leading Abu Talib to send him home safely.
key_points: Muhammad ﷺ invoked 'Bismillah' before eating and explicitly expressed his hatred for idols al-Lat and al-Uzza
Buhayra identified Khatam al-Nubuwwah (Seal of Prophethood) between the Prophet's ﷺ shoulders
Buhayra confirmed scriptural descriptions that the final prophet would be born an orphan
Abu Talib was warned that enemies in Sham might harm the boy out of envy, prompting him to send Muhammad ﷺ back to Makkah

chapters.title: Tending Sheep and Protection from Immorality
chapters.summary: Like all prophets before him, Muhammad ﷺ spent part of his youth tending sheep, which helped assist his poor uncle Abu Talib financially. During his youth in Makkah, Allah protected him from participating in or witnessing any worldly or sinful entertainment. On two separate occasions, when Muhammad ﷺ asked a fellow shepherd to guard his flock so he could observe evening wedding festivities in Makkah, Allah caused a deep sleep to overcome him until morning. As a result, he was preserved entirely from ever witnessing nighttime frivolities or immoral gatherings.
key_points: Hadith: 'There is no prophet except that he tended sheep' (Mā min nabiyyin illā wa-raʿā al-ghanam)
Muhammad ﷺ worked as a shepherd in Makkah to assist Abu Talib's large and poor household
On two occasions, young Muhammad ﷺ intended to observe local wedding celebrations
Allah protected him by causing him to sleep through the night until sunrise both times

chapters.title: Protection of Modesty and Noble Character
chapters.summary: Allah safeguarded the physical modesty and character of Muhammad ﷺ throughout his early life. While pagan practice often normalized public nakedness—such as performing tawaf unclad or stripping during heavy labor—Muhammad ﷺ was divine shielded. When his uncle al-Abbas suggested he place his waistcloth (izar) on his shoulder while carrying heavy stones for the Ka'bah, Muhammad ﷺ fainted before he could expose himself. Furthermore, even as a young child in Abu Talib's home, Muhammad ﷺ exhibited noble restraint during meal times, never rushing for food like other children, prompting Abu Talib to reserve a separate portion for him.
key_points: Pagan Arabs desensitized public nakedness, forcing impoverished pilgrims to perform tawaf unclothed
While carrying stones for the Ka'bah, al-Abbas suggested Muhammad ﷺ use his izar (waistcloth) as shoulder padding
Allah caused Muhammad ﷺ to faint before exposing his waistcloth, preserving his modesty
Young Muhammad ﷺ displayed noble eating habits (akhlaq), leading Abu Talib to set aside a dedicated portion of food for him

segments.translit: Bismillāhir-Raḥmānir-Raḥīm. Al-ḥamdu lillāhi Rabbil-ʿālamīn. Wa ṣallallāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn. Allāhumma ʿallimnā mā yanfaʿunā wa nfaʿnā bimā ʿallamtanā wa zidnā ʿilmā.

segments.text: Last week, when talking about the early childhood of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, we talked about how he moved from household to household.
And this is the way of an orphan, that when the father dies and the mother dies, then they are moved from household to household.
And this is what happened with the Prophet ﷺ.
So first, of course, for the first couple of years of his life, he was brought up in the desert with his wet nurse [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رضي الله عنها]].
And then she returned him to his mother after two years.
And he lived with his mother for another about four years, and then his mother died when [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was about six years old.
So a six-year-old boy, he already lost his father even before he was born, and now he's only six years old and he lost his mother as well.
Very difficult childhood that [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ had to go through.
After that, he stayed with his grandfather, who was the leader of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the head of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
So he stayed with [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], his grandfather, for another two years.
So from the age of six to eight, he stayed with his grandfather [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
And then [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] also died.
So now the Prophet ﷺ, he is an eight-year-old young boy, and he has been brought up already in three households.

First in the household of [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]] [[radiyallahu 'anha|رضي الله عنها]], then in the house of his own mother, [[Aminah bint Wahb|آمنة بنت وهب]], and then in the care of his grandfather [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
And now, at the age of eight, when the Prophet ﷺ was eight years old, [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] also passed away.
After this, the Prophet ﷺ went to live with his paternal uncle [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]].
[[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] was one of the most respected sons of [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]].
And he was the brother of the father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ.

The father of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, as we mentioned, his name was [[Abdullah ibn Abdul Muttalib|عبد الله بن عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]], and [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] ibn [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] was his brother.
So he was the paternal uncle of [[Rasulullah|رسول الله]] ﷺ, and he took him to care for him after [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] died.
He took in his eight-year-old nephew, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, and he treated him as if he was his own son.
He didn't treat him as an outsider, as a nephew. No, he treated him as his own son.
And he even used to call him, "[[ibni|ابني]], this is my son."
When people used to ask, "Who is this boy?" he would say, "This is my son."
So he had an immense love for this boy, and he treated him as if he was his own.
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ also grew very attached to [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]].
So they both loved each other, they both cared for each other, and they both respected each other very deeply.
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ stayed with [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] for a number of years.
When [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was 12 years old, so he had been living with [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] now for about four years...
He came into his household when he was eight years old, now he's about 12 years old.
So during these four years, they bonded, they became very close, and they both loved each other deeply.
So one summer, when [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was 12 years old, [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] was getting ready to make a business trip up to [[Sham|شام]].
[[Sham|شام]] is the Greater Syria area.
So he was getting ready one summer to make a trip up to [[Sham|شام]].
And it was well known that the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they used to take two major journeys every year: one journey in the summer and one journey in the winter.
In the summer, they would go up to [[Sham|شام]], the Greater Syria area, and do business there. And in the winter, they would go south to [[Yemen|اليمن]].
Because in the winter, [[Sham|شام]], it would be very, very freezing cold, so they wouldn't go there in the winter.
They would go to [[Yemen|اليمن]] in the winters, and they would go to [[Sham|شام]] in the summers. And Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala mentions this habit of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]:

The [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] has become accustomed, this has become a habit of them, to make these two journeys: [[rihlat ash-shitai was-sayf|رحلة الشتاء والصيف]], the journey of the winter and the journey of the summer.
The journey of the winter was to [[Yemen|اليمن]], and the journey of the summer was to [[Sham|شام]].
So [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], he's getting ready for the summer journey to go up to [[Sham|شام]].
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ is about 12 years old at this time, young boy still.
But he asks his uncle to allow him to accompany him on this journey.
He was excited and he said, "Can I go with you?"
And [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], he doesn't think that this is a good idea, and he tries to convince him, "No, let me go, you stay here in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]."
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ starts to cry because he really wants it, he really wants to go with his uncle.
So he starts to cry, and he asks his uncle again and again, "Please let me go with you, uncle. Please let me go with you."
And the sons of [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] are witnessing this, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ crying and asking [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] to let him accompany him on this journey.
So the sons of [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] tell [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, "Leave him, don't do this, just stay here with us, stay in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and let him go."
And [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] tells his sons, "No, don't worry about it, I will take him with me. I will take him with me."
So he tells his own sons to stop trying to tell [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ to stay, and he tells them that "I will take him, I will accompany him, I will let him accompany me on this journey."
So [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ is very happy and he's excited that he gets to go on this trip all the way to [[Sham|شام]].
And he has never actually left the greater [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] area since he came back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] from [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]]...

...since [[Halimah al-Sa'diyyah|حليمة السعدية]], his wet nurse, brought him back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to live with his mother when he was two years old, since that time he had never been on a trip like this.
He had never been outside the greater [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] area.
So he's very excited to take this first big journey in his life, and he's going to go with his uncle.
So he's happy and he's excited, and the caravan leaves [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], going towards [[Sham|شام]].
And the caravan, of course, it has a number of people from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], it's not just [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] and [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ.
No, it's a lot of people, a group of people from the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]] making that journey.
So they are moving on the way from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to [[Sham|شام]].
And on the way, on the pathway from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] to [[Sham|شام]], they passed by a monastery, a Christian monastery.
And in this Christian monastery, there lived some monks.
They used to live in the monastery, and they used to devote all of their time in worship.
They used to detach themselves from the [[dunya|دُنْيَا]] completely, and they used to just spend all of their time in worship.
And this is not something that Allah prescribed them to do.
This is something that they started to do as a form of extremism in leaving the [[dunya|دُنْيَا]], but this is not the way that Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala commanded them or commanded us.

Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala says about this type of way of living, just spending all of your time in the house of worship, only worshipping and having nothing at all to do with this [[dunya|دُنْيَا]]...
Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala says about that way of life:

This is a way of life, this [[rahbaniyyah|رَهْبَانِيَّة]], this monk lifestyle of cutting off the [[dunya|دُنْيَا]] completely, this is something that they innovated, that those people, they invented.
It is not something that was revealed to them by Allah Subhanahu wa Ta'ala.
[[ma katabnaha 'alayhim|مَا كَتَبْنَاهَا عَلَيْهِمْ]], "We did not prescribe this for them."
Anyhow, this was the way that these monks used to live.
They stayed in the monastery and they used to just spend all of their time worshipping, and they cut themselves off completely from the [[dunya|دُنْيَا]].
And the head of these monks in this particular monastery that the caravan passed by, the head of these monks was a man named [[Buhayra|بحيرى]].
And he noticed the caravan coming close, and he noticed...
Remember, this was the summer and the hot sun is out, right?
So [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] noticed that this caravan that's coming, there is a cloud that is covering the caravan, keeping it in the shade.
And wherever this caravan goes, the cloud is following it, keeping it in the shade, protecting it from the heat of the sun.
So when [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] noticed this, he realized that this is something special. This wouldn't just happen for anyone. There is something special about this particular caravan.
And many caravans had passed by in the previous years, right? And he never noticed anything special about them, but this one he noticed something special.
So the caravan stopped in a rest area near that monastery. Of course, it's a long journey from [[Makkah|مكّة]] to [[Sham|الشام]], so they have to make many stops on the way.
So they stopped at a point that was nearby this monastery.

And [[Buhayra|بحيرى]], he wanted more information about these people in this caravan because he realized there is something special here, because that cloud is following them and protecting them wherever they go.
So when he saw that they stopped nearby for rest,
he sent some of the people there in that monastery to go to that caravan and invite them for food—go to them and bring them back to the monastery,
invite them for a feast of food.
So a few of the people from the monastery, they go and they reach the caravan, and they say that, 'You are invited to come to the monastery and have some food with us.'
So those people—the people of the caravan, these members of the [[Quraysh|قريش]] who are with this caravan—they were kind of surprised that they were being invited for a feast,
because they had made this journey many times in the past.
Every summer they used to make this journey, they used to pass by the monastery so many times, and they were never invited in for food or anything.
So they said, 'This is strange, this is unusual. We're being invited for food today.'
'Okay, as long as we're invited, why don't we go ahead and have some food?' So they decided to accept the invitation.
But they didn't want to leave all of their stuff, all of their goods that they had with them in the caravan—they just didn't want to leave it unattended.
So they decided to accept the invitation and go into the monastery to eat food, but they decided that they have to leave one person there with the caravan to watch over the stuff.
And who was the youngest one there that they could tell to stay there and watch over the stuff? It was [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, the twelve-year-old boy.
So they said to him, 'Okay, we're going to go and accept this invitation and eat food.
You stay here at the caravan and make sure that nobody comes and takes our stuff.' So [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ said, 'Okay.' He agreed, he stayed there.
And the rest of the caravan, they went into the monastery to partake in this big feast that [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] had arranged.
Now [[Buhayra|بحيرى]], he invited them in for a specific purpose: to see the people and to see what was special about them.
So he started serving them personally and looking at each one of them carefully to see if there's anything special in any of them.
And he didn't notice anything special in any of them. He thought these are all normal people. So he asked, 'Did everyone from your caravan come here?
Did you leave anyone in the caravan?'
And then one of them said, 'Yeah, we're all here, everyone is here.' And then another guy said, 'No, no, no. Remember, we left the boy?
We left that young boy to watch over our stuff.'
And then a third man said, 'We left a young boy—we left this young boy, this orphan boy—while we are here enjoying food, and we left him with the caravan?
No, this is very bad. We should call him as well to come and have the food.'
So they sent some of their people to go to him and to bring him into the monastery to have some food with them as well.
So now [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, the twelve-year-old boy, he comes in. He comes inside, and [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] sees him. And he sees that yes, this boy, this is the boy.
There is something special about this boy.
So he sits down and [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] serves him some food. And he wants to have a conversation with him.
But before he starts conversation with him, he wants to just observe the boy a little bit, see what type of actions he has, see what is special about him.

So [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] just serves him some food. And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, before he starts eating the food, he says, '[[Bismillah|بسم الله]].' And [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] is amazed—look at this, he said, '[[Bismillah|بسم الله]].'
All of these other guys, when they started eating, some of them were saying, '[[Bismi al-Lat|باسم اللات]]', '[[Bismi al-Uzza|باسم العزى]]'—in the name of this god, in the name of that god,
in the name of this idol, in the name of that idol. But this boy, before he eats, he didn't mention anyone except Allah: '[[Bismillah|بسم الله]]', and then he starts to eat.
So [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] is impressed—this is a sign.
Then he asks the boy, 'What is your name?' And the boy replies, 'My name is [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]].'
Now [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] is even more happy because in their scriptures, in the previous revelations, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ is mentioned by his name.
So when he said his name is [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]], [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] became more convinced, 'Yes, this is the boy. This is a special boy.'
And then [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] wanted to test [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ. So he said, 'I want to ask you a question.'
And he noticed, before [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ came in, he noticed that these people of the [[Quraysh|قريش]], when they want to swear, when they want to swear, they say...

...'[[wa al-Lati wa al-Uzza|واللات والعزى]]' or '[[bi al-Lati wa al-Uzza|باللات والعزى]]'. They would swear by [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]], which were two of their false idols that they used to worship.
So when they would want to swear, make a statement and swear, they would say '[[bi al-Lat|باللات]]' or they would say '[[bi al-Uzza|بالعزى]]', and then they would make their statement.
So [[Buhayra|بحيرى]], he noticed this. Even though he was a Christian himself, he didn't believe in any of this stuff, he noticed that this is what they were doing.
So he wanted to test [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ in this regard as well. So he told [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, 'I want to ask you a question.' And he said...
'[[Sa'altuka bi-l-Lati wa-l-Uzza|سألتك باللات والعزى]].' He said, 'I ask you a question by [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]].'

And then [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, when he heard [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] mention [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]], he said, '[[La tuhallifni bi-l-Lati wa-l-Uzza, fa-Wallahi ma abghadtu shay'an bughdi lahuma|لا تحلفني باللات والعزى، فوالله ما أبغضت شيئًا بغضي لهما]].'
He said, 'Do not speak to me in terms of swearing by [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]], because [[Wallahi|والله]], I swear by Allah, I do not hate anything more than I hate these two.
I don't hate anything more than I hate [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]].'
Now look at this, this is actually amazing.

[[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ growing up in [[Makkah|مكّة]], growing up among the [[Quraysh|قريش]], where they all worship—or most of them worship—these two idols, they worship [[al-Lat|اللات]] and they worship [[al-Uzza|العزى]], and they worship other idols as well.
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ is growing up in these households where these idols are worshipped. He grew up with [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]]...
...and [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] was from the people who worshipped these idols as well.
He grew up with [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]]—he's living with [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] during this time even—and [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] worshipped these idols as well.
So this idol worship is all around him, even from his own family members, yet still Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سبحانه وتعالى]] is the One who protected him from ever falling into [[shirk|شرك]],
from ever falling into any type of association of partners with Allah. Allah protected him.
So he said, '[[Wallahi ma abghadtu shay'an bughdi lahuma|والله ما أبغضت شيئًا بغضي لهما]].
I have never hated anything in my life more than I hate [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]], so don't talk to me about that.'
So [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] is very happy to hear these answers, very happy. That was his test, and [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ passed this test perfectly.
Then he said, 'Okay, I won't ask you by swearing by [[al-Lat|اللات]] and [[al-Uzza|العزى]], [[sa'altuka bi-Llah|سألتك بالله]], I ask you by Allah.'
Then [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ said, 'Yes, this is what I want, this is okay.'

And then he started asking him some personal questions. And every answer that [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ gave him increased [[Buhayra|بحيرى]]'s certainty that this is the Prophet that we are waiting for.
He is going to become that Prophet that we are waiting for.
So [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] is very happy with all of his answers. He asks him some personal questions, he asks him some questions about what kind of dreams he has,
and all of the answers increased the certainty of [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] that this boy is going to grow up to be the Messenger of Allah that we are waiting for.
Finally, [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] had one more request to [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ. He said, 'Do you mind, can you just uncover your back? Let me see your back, the skin on your back.'
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, twelve-year-old boy...
Okay, if you want to see, go ahead, see.

And the reason why [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] asked this question was because it has been revealed in the previous revelations that this messenger that's going to come, he will have [[Khatam al-Nubuwwah|خاتم النبوة]], the seal of prophethood on his back.
And there are many ahadith that mention the seal of the prophethood that was on the back of the Prophet ﷺ between his shoulders.
It's a raised piece of skin.
There was a raised piece of skin on his back between his shoulders that had some thick hair on it, and that was the seal of prophethood.
And it was mentioned in the previous scriptures, the previous revelations, that this prophet, he is going to have this on his back.
And [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] knew this, he was a knowledgeable person.
He knew this, so he said, after all of the questions and answers that they went through back and forth, after he was satisfied with all of them, he said, 'I just need to see this one last thing.'
He wanted to make it certain by seeing that.
So when [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ let him see his back, he saw exactly, it was there.
And then he knew for sure 100%, this is the boy. This boy is going to grow up to be the messenger that we are waiting for.
Then he went to [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] and he said, 'Who is this boy for you? Who is this boy in relation to you?'
And as we mentioned earlier before, [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], he used to call [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ 'Ibni' (my son).
Even though he was his nephew, he used to call him 'my son', because he treated him as a son.
So when [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] asked [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], 'Who is this boy to you?'
He said, 'He is my son.'
And then [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] was shocked and surprised. He was like, 'No, no, this boy, his father can't be alive.'
There is no way that the father of this boy is alive, because amongst the descriptions of the messenger that was to come was that he was an orphan.
And [[Buhayra|بحيرى]], he's knowledgeable, he knows about these scriptures, he has read them, and he knows that the boy is an orphan.
So when [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] said, 'This is my son', [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] said, 'No way, he can't be your son. This boy does not have a father that is alive.'
So when he asked [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] again, 'Tell me exactly, who is he to you?'
He said, 'Okay, yeah, he's actually my nephew, but, you know, he lives with me and I'm bringing him up, so he's like my son.'
He said, 'Okay, okay, now it makes sense. You're not really his father.'
So [[Buhayra|بحيرى]] was 100% convinced that this is the boy who is going to grow up to be the messenger, the prophet that they are all waiting for.
So he tells [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], he says, 'Do not take him to [[Sham|شام]].'
Do not let him complete this journey with you to [[Sham|شام]], because in [[Sham|شام]] there are the Jews who, when they see this boy, they are going to recognize him.
Just like I recognized him, they're going to recognize him as well, because they know his description in the [[Tawrah|توراة]].
They're going to know that he is the boy who is going to become the Messenger of Allah.
But once they realize that he is from the Arabs, that he is not from [[Bani Isra'il|بني إسرائيل]], he is not from the children of [[Ya'qub|يعقوب]], once they realize that,
they're not going to be happy, and they will kill him out of jealousy. So do not let him go to [[Sham|شام]].
So [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] hearing all of this, he gets very scared. Like, what is all of this strange stuff that is happening?
This man [[Buhayra|بحيرى]], you know, he invites us for food, and then he's talking with all of this talk. He's very afraid.
So he decides, 'Okay, I'm not going to take him to [[Sham|شام]].'
And he arranges for him to be escorted back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
While the rest of them complete the journey, [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] arranges for some of the people from the caravan to take [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ back into [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
So he didn't get to complete that journey to [[Sham|شام]].
So we see here that the signs of the Messenger ﷺ, they were there from his early childhood.
From the beginning, even from his birth, there were so many signs that pointed to the fact that there is something very special about this boy.
And when he went back to [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the signs that showed the fact that he was special, they continued and they got more and more and more.
One of the signs that the Prophet ﷺ was protected by Allah from anything, from doing anything bad even before he became a prophet,
was that Allah Subḥānahu wa Taʿālā protected him from ever witnessing or ever being part of any type of immorality.
When the Prophet ﷺ went to live with [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] was very, very, very poor.
[[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] was very poor, and we mentioned last week the reasons why the leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]],
like [[Abdul Muttalib|عَبْد الْمُطَّلِب]] and [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] and the other brothers of [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], we mentioned why they were poor,
even though they were the most honorable family and the most respected family, and they were the leaders of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
we mentioned that they were still poor because they used to spend all of their wealth in service of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]].
And [[hujjaj|حجاج]] would come from all over the place, and these leaders of the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they would take their responsibility of taking care of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]] very seriously,
so they would spend all of their money to take care of these [[hujjaj|حجاج]].
Even though they were earning good income, they would spend all of it to take care of the [[hujjaj|حجاج]]. So that's why they were poor.

segments.translit: Mā min nabiyyin illā wa-raʿā al-ghanam Total text translated below in next segment: There is no prophet except that he tended sheep.

segments.text: There is no prophet except that at some point in his life he tended to sheep. He took care of sheep, every single prophet.
And the Prophet ﷺ, [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ, was no exception to that.
He actually did that as well, and by doing that he earned some money to help his uncle take care of the household.
Now, when [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ was a young man, and one of these days he was taking care of the sheep on the outskirts of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
and the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] from time to time they used to have different types of occasions and different celebrations, they used to have weddings and such.
And in these parties, these wedding parties, a lot of bad stuff used to go on. And sadly, even today in many wedding parties a lot of bad stuff goes on.
So even in the time of the Prophet ﷺ, before he became a prophet when he was a young man, some of those celebrations in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], those weddings in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]],
a lot of bad stuff used to go on there, singing, dancing, all of these type of things.
And the Prophet ﷺ never attended one of these things. He never saw it, he never witnessed it at all.
So one day he was on the outskirts of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] tending some sheep, and there was a companion of his also tending some sheep as well, you know.
And they could see that, you know, a wedding was going on in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. They could see that some wedding is going on tonight in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
And [[Muhammad|مُحَمَّد]] ﷺ had never seen any of this type of thing in his life, he had never seen what happens at these parties or anything.
So out of curiosity, he was interested to go and just see what it's all about.
So he told that other companion of his who was there tending the sheep, he said, 'Can you look over my sheep tonight?
Can you take care of my sheep as well tonight?
I have never attended, you know, one of these wedding parties in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], and I'm interested, you know, to see what it's all about.' So the guy said, 'Yeah, sure, no problem.
I'll take care of your sheep, you go ahead.'
So he wanted to go, but he became very, very sleepy. He became very, very tired, and he fell asleep.
And the only thing that woke him up was the heat of the sun the next day.
So he slept throughout the whole night, he missed the whole party, morning came, and the sun came, and he woke up by the heat of the sun.
So he missed it completely.
So he went back, and he told his friend, 'Yeah, I mean, I was going to go, but I fell asleep and I missed it.' Okay.
Later, another time, after some time, the same situation happened again. There was a wedding there, and he asked the friend, he asked the man, 'Can you look over my sheep?
You know, I'm going to go this time and check it out.' He said, 'Yeah, sure, go ahead.'
The same exact thing happened to him again.
He felt very drowsy, very sleepy, he fell asleep, and he only woke up by the feeling of the heat of the sun on his body. Both times Allah...

saved him from even witnessing any type of immoral behavior taking place. This was the special protection that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] kept on him. [[SubhanAllah|سُبْحَانَ اللهِ]].
Another one of the protections that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] gave His Messenger ﷺ even before he became a prophet...
...was the fact that he was never exposed. His body was never exposed for the people to see.
And the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], nakedness amongst them was something that was considered very normal.
Many of the people used to actually make [[tawaf|طَوَاف]] around the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]] naked, without clothes.
And what was the reasoning behind this? [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]], they used to come in from all over the place.
And the people of [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], they wanted to think of a way where they could earn some money from these [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]].
So they made a rule that if anyone wants to make [[tawaf|طَوَاف]] around the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], they have to only do it with clothing that is purchased in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]].
You can't bring your own clothes from whatever country you come from and make [[tawaf|طَوَاف]].
If you want to make [[tawaf|طَوَاف]] of the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]], you have to do it in our special clothes from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]] itself.
And who are the ones who were selling those clothes? It was the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]]. So they thought that, okay, this is a way we can make some money.

So whoever could afford it, whoever had enough money to afford these clothes from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], they would pay the [[Quraysh|قُرَيْش]], and they would get these clothing, these pieces of clothing, and wear it and make [[tawaf|طَوَاف]].
Okay, but not all of the [[hujjaj|حُجَّاج]] are rich. They don't all have so much money. A number of them could not afford it.
So they said, 'Okay, if you can't afford it, if you can't afford this clothing from [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], you have to make [[tawaf|طَوَاف]] without any clothes, naked.'
So many people, they used to make [[tawaf|طَوَاف]] naked. And the fact that people were always around the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]] doing [[tawaf|طَوَاف]] without any clothes...
...it made this sight something very normal to the Arabs there. They would see it every day, and they became desensitized to it.
It became something that's like an everyday thing, normal thing. Nobody thought much about it.
So nakedness became like a common thing, a normal thing, amongst these Arabs.

Also, when they were doing some heavy work, when they would do heavy work like lifting stones and stuff like that, you know, to minimize the heat of the sun, they would take off their clothes sometimes too.
Because [[Makkah|مَكَّة]], it gets very hot, so they thought, 'Okay, let's take off our clothes when we're doing this work, it won't be as hot, at least.'
So they would take off their clothes, you know, when they're doing heavy lifting and heavy work sometimes.
It was something very normal amongst them. So one day, the Prophet ﷺ, he was helping his uncles do some work near the [[Ka'bah|كَعْبَة]]. They were lifting some heavy stones.
And the Prophet ﷺ was helping in that as well. And the Prophet ﷺ, of course, he had his waistcloth, his [[izar|إِزَار]] on, right?
And he was lifting these heavy stones on his shoulders, right?
So his uncle [[al-Abbas|الْعَبَّاس]] he said to him, he said, 'Why don't you take off your [[izar|إِزَار]], take off the waistcloth and put it on your shoulders...'
'...instead of carrying the big stone like that right on your shoulders, take your waistcloth and put it on your shoulder and carry the stone on that so it won't really hurt your shoulder.
You can have like a barrier between the stone and your shoulder. So why don't you take off the [[izar|إِزَار]] and put it on?'
That was something that was very normal amongst them, you know. Nobody thought it was a big deal.
So the Prophet ﷺ says, when he said that and when I thought about doing it, when I was ready to actually do it, the Prophet ﷺ fainted.
Before he could take off his waistcloth, he fainted. Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] caused him to faint.
So Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] protected him from ever exposing his body to anyone, to the people.
So this just shows how Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] was with him and protected him from everything, every single step of the way, throughout his whole life.
Another example is that Allah [[Subhanahu wa Ta'ala|سُبْحَانَهُ وَتَعَالَى]] kept the manners and the character of the Prophet ﷺ at the topmost level, even when he was a little child.
Not only when he was an adult, but even from his young childhood, his [[akhlaq|أَخْلَاق]], his manners, were the best of manners.
An example of this was when food would be served out in the household of [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]].
And we mentioned that [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], he was a poor man and he had many children.
So when the food would be prepared and when the food would be served, all of those children, they would jump on that food and try to get whatever they could. Right?
This is a common thing for children to do.
When food is served, everybody wants to get whatever they can. And there were a lot of them, so each one of them wanted to make sure they get something.
But Muhammad ﷺ would never participate in this. He would watch them do it, he would stay away, let them take whatever they want to take and leave.
Then he would go, if there's anything leftover, he would eat it. If there's nothing leftover, he will go to sleep hungry.
But he would never participate in jumping on the food and taking it like that, like his cousins were doing.
From a young age, this was his character, this was his piety.
And nobody noticed that this was happening for a long time, that some nights he was going to sleep hungry because of this. People didn't notice it.
But then after some time, [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] started to notice it. [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]] noticed that, yeah, when they're all going on the food, he's staying away.
And if there's any food left, he takes it; if there's nothing left, he quietly, without complaining, he goes to sleep hungry. A little child.
So [[Abu Talib|أَبُو طَالِب]], he felt very sad about this.
And he said to the people who were preparing the food, he said, 'Okay, when you make the food, just keep one part separate.
Keep one part separate and serve out the rest of the food so the boys can eat it, so the kids can eat it.
And keep one part separate and we'll give it to Muhammad ﷺ separately, because he doesn't participate in this jumping on the food like the other kids are doing.'
So he started to do that. So this shows the greatness of Muhammad ﷺ even from his childhood.
[[insha'Allah|إِنْ شَاءَ اللهُ]] next week, we will continue to talk about some events that happened in the young adult life of Muhammad ﷺ in [[Makkah|مَكَّة]]. [[Wallahu a'lam|وَاللهُ أَعْلَم]].

segments.translit: Wa ṣallā Allāhu wa sallama wa bāraka ʿalā nabiyyinā Muḥammadin wa ʿalā ālihi wa ṣaḥbihi ajmaʿīn.
